positions.commentary: Amazon is a great brand with a narrow distribution of outcomes where the speaker has high confidence in consistently good experiences.
Netflix has a much higher dispersion of outcomes where most content is terrible but some is amazing, creating excitement for discovery.

thesis: This episode contrasts the investment characteristics of Amazon and Netflix by highlighting Amazon's narrow distribution of outcomes and high confidence in consistent performance versus Netflix's high dispersion of outcomes driven by a mix of terrible and amazing content.

claims.claim: Amazon is a great brand with a narrow distribution of outcomes where the speaker has high confidence in consistently good experiences.
claims.quote: I mean, I think Amazon's a great example of this. Like, they built a brand that as a consumer, I mean, I love Amazon. I know that they're never going to cheat me.

claims.claim: Netflix has a much higher dispersion of outcomes where most content is terrible but some is amazing, creating excitement for discovery.
claims.quote: So Netflix, obviously has a much higher dispersion by which I mean, we'll, we'll just focus on Netflix originals, right? So they have so much much much content now. And unlike, and most of it's crap. Most of it's, most of it's probably crap.
